# Sango

> Sango is an operator-grade edge diagnostics CLI that analyzes a web endpoint in a single command: TLS, HTTP protocols, security headers, latency, and technology stack.

Sango (珊瑚, "coral") is a read-only command-line tool for operators and developers who want to know whether a web edge is sane, observable, and survivable. Point it at a URL (`sango https://example.com`) and it inspects the TLS certificate chain, expiry, cipher and ALPN, detects HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support, checks security headers such as HSTS, CSP, COOP/COEP and X-Frame-Options, breaks latency down into DNS, TCP, TLS and TTFB, and reports judgments rather than raw data. Output is available as pretty text, JSON, or a compact single line, and the exit code reflects the health of the endpoint (0 healthy or degraded, 1 unhealthy, 2 unknown). All probes are standard, safe HTTP and TLS operations. It is written in Rust and installs with `cargo install sango` or `curl -fsSL getsango.raskell.io | sh`. The website also runs a reduced, browser-based demo compiled to WebAssembly that checks headers, SEO, AEO and content of a URL. Sango is free and open source under the Apache 2.0 licence.

## Links
